nodes.title: Combined (Joint) Equation of Lines
points: If u ≡ a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and v ≡ a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0 represent two straight lines, their combined equation is u · v = 0.
To separate a combined second-degree equation into individual lines: factorize the quadratic expression into two linear factors.
Combined equation of coordinate axes: xy = 0.
Lines parallel to coordinate axes passing through (h, k): (x − h)(y − k) = 0 ⟹ xy − ky − hx + hk = 0.

nodes.title: Homogeneous Equation of Degree Two
points: A homogeneous equation of degree 2 in x and y has the form: ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0.
It represents a pair of straight lines PASSING THROUGH THE ORIGIN (0, 0).
Nature of Lines depends on discriminant (h² − ab):
1. If h² − ab > 0: Lines are real and distinct.
2. If h² − ab = 0: Lines are real and coincident (identical).
3. If h² − ab < 0: Lines are imaginary (not real, intersect only at origin).

nodes.title: Slopes of Lines & Auxiliary Equation
points: Let the lines be y = m₁x and y = m₂x (passing through origin).
Dividing ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 by x² gives the Auxiliary Equation: bm² + 2hm + a = 0.
Roots of this quadratic are the slopes m₁ and m₂.
Sum of slopes: m₁ + m₂ = −2h / b.
Product of slopes: m₁ · m₂ = a / b.
Difference of slopes: |m₁ − m₂| = √[(m₁ + m₂)² − 4m₁m₂] = [2√(h² − ab)] / |b|.

nodes.title: Acute Angle Between Lines (ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0)
points: Acute angle θ between the lines ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 is given by: tanθ = |[2√(h² − ab)] / (a + b)|.
Condition for Perpendicular Lines (θ = 90°): a + b = 0 ⟹ Coefficient of x² + Coefficient of y² = 0.
Condition for Coincident / Parallel Lines (θ = 0°): h² − ab = 0 ⟹ h² = ab.
If a + b = 0, lines are mutually perpendicular, irrespective of the value of h.

nodes.title: General Second Degree Equation in x and y
points: General equation: ax² + 2hxy + by² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0.
Condition to represent a pair of straight lines: Determinant Δ = 0 AND h² − ab ≥ 0.
Determinant form: Δ = [[a, h, g], [h, b, f], [g, f, c]] = abc + 2fgh − af² − bg² − ch² = 0.
Angle between lines represented by general equation is the SAME as that for ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0: tanθ = |[2√(h² − ab)] / (a + b)|.
Lines are perpendicular if a + b = 0; parallel if h² − ab = 0.

formulas.label: Matrix determinant form
formulas.expr: det [[a, h, g], [h, b, f], [g, f, c]] = 0

nodes.title: Point of Intersection & Parallel Lines Distance
points: Point of intersection (x₀, y₀) of lines represented by general equation:
x₀ = (hf − bg) / (ab − h²); y₀ = (gh − af) / (ab − h²).
Shortcut: Solve partial derivatives ∂S/∂x = 0 (ax + hy + g = 0) and ∂S/∂y = 0 (hx + by + f = 0) simultaneously.
Distance between parallel lines (h² = ab, bg² = af²):

nodes.title: Angle Bisectors of Pair of Lines
points: The combined equation of angle bisectors of lines ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 is: (x² − y²) / (a − b) = xy / h.
Cross multiplying: h(x² − y²) = (a − b)xy ⟹ hx² − (a − b)xy − hy² = 0.
Properties of angle bisectors:
(1) Coefficient of x² + Coefficient of y² = h + (−h) = 0 ⟹ The two angle bisectors are ALWAYS mutually perpendicular.
(2) If a = b, the bisectors are simply x² − y² = 0 ⟹ y = ±x.

nodes.title: Homogenization of Curves (Lines to Origin)
points: To find the joint equation of lines joining the origin (0, 0) to points of intersection of a line lx + my + n = 0 and a second-degree curve ax² + 2hxy + by² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0:
Step 1: Write line equation in terms of 1: (lx + my) / (−n) = 1.
Step 2: Multiply degree-1 terms (2gx + 2fy) by [(lx + my) / (−n)]¹.
Step 3: Multiply degree-0 term c by [(lx + my) / (−n)]².
Result: ax² + 2hxy + by² + (2gx + 2fy)[(lx + my)/(−n)] + c[(lx + my)/(−n)]² = 0.
This yields a homogeneous second-degree equation representing the two lines from origin.

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Theorems & Derivations
points: Board Favourite #1: Theorem: Prove that every homogeneous equation of degree two ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 represents a pair of lines passing through origin if h² − ab ≥ 0.
Board Favourite #2: Theorem: Prove that the acute angle θ between lines ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 is given by tanθ = |[2√(h² − ab)] / (a + b)|.
Board Favourite #3: Deduce conditions for lines to be perpendicular (a + b = 0) and coincident (h² − ab = 0).
Board Favourite #4: Find p and q if 2x² + 4xy − py² + 4x + qy + 1 = 0 represents a pair of perpendicular lines.
Board Favourite #5: Find the joint equation of lines joining origin to points of intersection of a line and a circle.

nodes.title: MHT-CET Shortcuts, Slope Relations & 10-Second Hacks
points: If one line is perpendicular to px + qy + r = 0: its slope is q/p. Substitute m = q/p into auxiliary equation bm² + 2hm + a = 0.
If one line bisects angle between coordinate axes: m = ±1 ⟹ b(±1)² + 2h(±1) + a = 0 ⟹ (a + b)² = 4h².
If lines are at 60°: tan 60° = √3 ⟹ |2√(h² − ab) / (a + b)| = √3 ⟹ (a + 3b)(3a + b) = 4h².
Area of Equilateral Triangle formed by ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 and lx + my + n = 0: Area = n² / [√3 (al² + 2hlm + bm²)].
Product of perpendiculars from (x₁, y₁) to lines ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0: d₁d₂ = |ax₁² + 2hx₁y₁ + by₁²| / √[(a − b)² + 4h²].
